A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Robo-SGG and contain readable text, equations, tables, and figures supporting comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix; both reference supplementary material that is not included. The assessment covers the supplied content only.

before.justification: v1 reports original Robo-SGG experiments on VG/VG-C and GQA/GQA-C, including baseline comparisons, component ablations, corruption-severity tests, and timing measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and adds component controls, distribution-shift and bounding-box robustness tests, repeated-run information, and runtime/memory measurements.

M1.justification: The central NRM attention procedure changes. v1 Eqs. 10–13 normalize Gaussian-derived attention across pixels for each object and sum weighted residuals across objects. v2 Eqs. 9–10 normalize distances over objects at each spatial location, then take the maximum object attention as a residual mask. This changes normalization and aggregation, while IN, gated fusion, and the training loss remain.

E1.justification: VG/GQA, their corrupted counterparts, and the three SGG tasks remain. v2 Table 5 substantially broadens test scenarios beyond the original image corruptions: perturbed detected bounding boxes, StyleID-generated image style changes, and zero-shot label-distribution shifts. These change input conditions and generalization requirements without introducing a new named dataset.

E2.justification: RelTR, previously cited but not evaluated, becomes an evaluated one-stage comparator in v2 Figure 4. EGTR, MOTIFS, VCTree, VTransE, HiKER, DPL, SNR, and DDPG remain in their corresponding comparisons. v2 also introduces addition and concatenation alternatives in the fusion comparison.

E3.justification: The EGTR comparison changes from SGDet R@20 reporting to mR@50/mR@100. New experiments introduce component controls, bounding-box perturbations of ±30% of width/height, style transfer, and zero-shot evaluation. Figure 2's caption also changes validation from clean to corrupted images, although its diagram still labels validation as clean; the actual validation procedure is therefore uncertain.

E4.justification: v2 adds NRM-only ablations, addition/concatenation/gating comparisons, centroid-versus-box attention tests, detection-noise and distribution-shift robustness tests, and gating-coefficient analysis. It also adds failure interpretation and per-corruption/error analyses. The original severity and denoising comparisons remain, but the Gaussian-noise desk example and three feature-map corruption examples are removed.

E5.justification: v1 provides no experimental repeated-run or uncertainty reporting. v2 Section 4.2 first reports three random seeds for MOTIFS+Ours on SGCls and a standard deviation below 0.01. This is limited new uncertainty reporting; it does not establish an increase over any previously undisclosed run count.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for the new controls, robustness scenarios, profiling, and RelTR, including corrupted SGDet mR@50 of 3.4 versus 3.7 with Robo-SGG. Table 1 changes DPL+Ours corrupted SGDet mR@100 from 6.4 to 5.7 and VCTree+Ours clean SGDet mR@50 from 7.2 to 7.3, while most existing scores remain. EGTR results use different metrics and cannot establish a same-setting performance change.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 substantively revises the mathematical definition of layout attention and structural restitution, replacing spatial normalization and summation with object normalization and a maximum-derived mask. This is a localized formal revision. The scene-graph, instance-normalization, and gating definitions otherwise remain, and neither version provides theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: The main plug-and-play NRM/LEE and state-of-the-art claims remain. v2 qualifies the earlier domain-invariant and unchangeable-layout claims as relative robustness compared with texture or color, and emphasizes adaptive fusion of existing coordinate embeddings. Advertised mR@50 gains change from 5.6%, 8.0%, and 6.5% to 6.3%, 11.1%, and 8.0%.

C2.justification: v2 substantially revises the explanation of reliability: bounding boxes can themselves become noisy, gating should balance unreliable spatial and visual cues, and centroids are interpreted as less sensitive to detection noise. It newly explains weaker blur improvements through lost structural boundaries and discusses near/behind annotation ambiguity in a failure case. These qualify v1's stronger layout-invariance narrative.

D1.justification: v2 specifies coordinate normalization to [0,1], feature alignment, Faster R-CNN/Transformer proposal handling, and severity level 5 for Table 1. It adds per-iteration runtime/memory information but removes explicit VG/GQA vocabulary and split descriptions and earlier total-training-time measurements. These are documentation changes rather than evidence of changed dataset splits. Both versions still promise future code/model release.

R1.justification: The related-work coverage is substantially contracted, dropping the earlier video/3D/AR discussion while adding layout-analysis, style-transfer, detector, and visual-commonsense references. Positioning against key predecessors also changes: coordinate embeddings are explicitly credited to prior work, SHA is contrasted through fusion under unreliable detections, and HiKER is criticized for dependence on external knowledge graphs.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and method explanations are extensively rewritten and condensed. Object/predicate framework descriptions are merged, and a new Section 5 reorganizes efficiency, severity, denoising, and additional analyses. The title and author block also change. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: v2 changes typography and page organization, redraws introductory/framework figures, restructures tables, adds a one-stage comparison chart and three tables, removes one qualitative example, and reduces the multi-corruption feature visualization to a focused contrast example. The severity plot and DDPG table are retained as Figure 6 and Table 7; their relocation is not new evidence.

improvement.justification: The NRM-only and fusion controls and perturbed-box tests in v2 Tables 2, 4, and 5 strengthen component attribution and address the reliability of layout inputs. More qualified claims and limited seed reporting also improve credibility. However, removed split documentation and the newly inconsistent validation description in Figure 2 limit the overall gain.
